ei.title: Fear of Flying and the Odds
ei.subject: 9월_2023 고1 모의고사
ei.lesson: Fear of Flying and the Odds

fullPassage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① terrified — control — instills: 사람들이 비행을 '겁내고', '통제력'의 부족이 두려움을 '불어넣는다'는 원문 흐름과 완전히 일치하는 조합

❌ ② relaxed — control — instills: (A) relaxed(편안한)는 terrified(겁먹은)의 반의어라 비행 공포 맥락에 부적절

❌ ③ terrified — freedom — instills: (B) freedom(자유)은 control(통제)의 반의어라 '통제력 부족'이라는 원문과 맞지 않음

❌ ④ terrified — control — removes: (C) removes(없애다)는 instills(불어넣다)의 반의어라 '두려움을 불어넣는다'는 맥락과 반대
det.tip: terrified↔relaxed, control↔freedom, instills↔removes

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① partly — emotion — logic: (A) partly(부분적으로)는 solely(오로지)와 뜻이 달라 '오로지 감정에만 근거한다'는 원문과 맞지 않음

✅ ② solely — emotion — logic: 운전 결정이 '오로지' '감정'에 근거하며 '논리'가 아니라는 원문과 완전 일치

❌ ③ solely — reason — logic: (B) reason(이성)은 뒤의 logic과 의미가 겹쳐 감정 vs 논리의 대비가 무너짐

❌ ④ solely — emotion — feeling: (C) feeling(느낌)은 emotion과 의미가 겹쳐 '감정이 아닌 논리'라는 대비가 사라짐
det.tip: solely = only(오로지). emotion(감정) ↔ logic(논리)의 대비가 핵심

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① excitement — facts — feelings: (A) excitement(흥분)은 사람들이 피하려는 anxiety(불안)와 뜻이 달라 부적절

❌ ② anxiety — guesses — feelings: (B) guesses(추측)는 facts(사실)와 반대라 '사실에 근거하라'는 원문과 맞지 않음

det.tip: anxiety(불안) ↔ 흥분/편안, facts(사실) ↔ feelings(느낌)

✅ ③ (A) 확률 — (B) 불화: (A) 사고로 죽을 '확률', (B) be at odds = '불화/의견 대립' — 다의어 의미가 문맥에 정확히 맞음

❌ ④ (A) 역경 — (B) 승산: 두 의미 모두 문맥과 어긋남
det.tip: odds: (확률) the odds of ~ / (불화) be at odds with ~

❌ ② insist: 주장하다 — 정의와 다름

❌ ③ install: 설치하다 — 소리는 비슷하나 의미가 다름

✅ ④ instill: (생각·감정을) 마음속에 서서히 심어 주다 — 정의에 정확히 부합
det.tip: instill fear = 두려움을 심어 주다/불어넣다

questions.passage: Many people are __________ (terrify) to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.analysis: 정답: terrified — 'be동사 + 감정 형용사' 자리. 사람이 감정을 '느끼는' 상태이므로 과거분사형 형용사 terrified(겁먹은)가 알맞음. terrifying(무섭게 하는)은 사물·대상을 꾸밀 때 씀.
det.tip: 감정 동사: 사람이 느끼면 -ed(terrified), 대상이 그렇게 만들면 -ing(terrifying)

questions.passage: But their decision to drive is __________ (base) solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 (1단어) (영어로) 쓰시오.

det.analysis: 정답: based — 'be동사 + 과거분사'의 수동태 구조. 결정이 감정에 '근거해지는' 것이므로 be based on(~에 근거하다) 형태가 되어 based가 알맞음.
det.tip: be based on ~ = ~에 근거하다 (수동태 표현)

questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds __________? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on facts, not just feelings.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① in your favor: 원문 일치 — 위험을 감수한다면 확률을 '자신에게 유리하게' 두고 싶을 것이라는 맥락

❌ ② out of control: 통제 불능인 — 앞부분 소재이나 이 자리에는 부적절

❌ ③ against the odds: 역경을 무릅쓰고 — 확률을 유리하게 하려는 맥락과 반대

❌ ④ by pure chance: 순전히 우연으로 — 논리·확률로 판단하라는 글의 취지와 어긋남
det.tip: the odds in your favor = 자신에게 유리한 확률

questions.passage: Many people are terrified to fly in airplanes. Often, this fear stems from a lack of control. The pilot is in control, not the passengers, and this lack of control instills fear. Many potential passengers are so afraid they choose to drive great distances to get to a destination instead of flying. But their decision to drive is based solely on emotion, not logic. Logic says that statistically, the odds of dying in a car crash are around 1 in 5,000, while the odds of dying in a plane crash are closer to 1 in 11 million. If you're going to take a risk, especially one that could possibly involve your well-being, wouldn't you want the odds in your favor? However, most people choose the option that will cause them the least amount of anxiety. Pay attention to the thoughts you have about taking the risk and make sure you're basing your decision on __________, not just feelings.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① feelings: 느낌 — 바로 뒤 'not just feelings'와 모순되어 부적절

✅ ② facts: 원문 일치 — '느낌이 아닌(not just feelings) 사실에 근거해 결정하라'는 대비 구조

❌ ③ fears: 두려움 — 감정의 일종이라 'not feelings'와 충돌

❌ ④ emotions: 감정 — feelings와 같은 부류라 대비가 무너짐
det.tip: base your decision on facts, not just feelings = 느낌이 아닌 사실에 근거하라
